utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Oh, there was. Oh, I apologise. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll need to go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We need -- we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Just before the witness comes in, we had received the 65 ter summary for this witness which had very simply provided that this former OTP investigator, Mr. Bruce Bursik, would be testifying about statements of Momir Nikolic, how they were created and who provided what during the interview process. Yesterday at ten to 4.00, we received a proofing note which the Chamber, I believe, was copied on and which provided us with one small issue that would be covered during the testimony but really not that much more. I spoke to Mr. Lukic just this morning, and he did provide me with further details about what topics would be covered with Mr. Bursik today. And we are prepared to proceed on the basis of what Mr. Lukic has told me this morning, but we will do so carefully and I'll just have to assess where we're at the conclusion of the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's a -- that's a caveat for --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I can just respond briefly, Your Honours. There is nothing unknown to the Prosecution that it was their investigation -- investigator, those are their documents, and we saw Mr. Bursik for the first time yesterday. So as soon as we were able to provide the Prosecution with anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. The only thing Ms. Hasan says is that if we're taken by surprise, but we do not know yet, we'll assess that at the end of the examination-in-chief, we reserve our position as how to proceed. That's what she says. Now, there's a fair chance that after the examination-in-chief she says there's nothing, let's just proceed. So, therefore, why start a battle on matters where there may be no need for a battle? At the same time, Mr. Lukic, to say that if it's an OTP investigator you would know everything. That, of course, may be true; may not be true. It depends on what you're talking about. The Chamber doesn't know. Let's wait and see. I do understand that you say we are not taking the OTP in any way by surprise. Let's wait and see where we are at the end of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then are you ready to call Mr. Bursik?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bursik, I presume.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. May I invite you to make that declaration, of which the text is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bursik. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll find Mr. Lukic to your left, almost standing. Now standing. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bursik.

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Morning, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us your first and last name and then check if it's correctly spelled.

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: My name is Bruce Bursik. It's correctly spelt.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: My date of birth is the 3rd of August, 1969.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will make pauses after your answers so we give the opportunity to the translators to translate to other languages. Can you tell us when did you join the OTP office at this Tribunal, please.

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I joined the OTP on the 1st of September, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when did you stop working for the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I stopped working in March 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly how many suspects did you interview working for the OTP of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't recall exactly -- the exact amount but it would be in excess of 20 suspect interviews that we had, not necessarily every one of them being persons that were indicted but treated as suspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With so much experience, do you think you have a good feel for the truthfulness of the witness?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And does your role as an investigator involve judging the truthfulness of the statement told to you?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: My role as an investigator is to uncover the truth and part of that process is to try and establish whether a witness is telling the truth or not, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was your perception of the demeanour of Momir Nikolic during your interview or your interviews with him?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: In the beginning stages of our interviews, bearing in mind we had many interviews with him, I found him to be quite evasive, and then it reached a point where he started to give us more information, which seemed to be in line with what we believed happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, at the end, you believed what he said, or most part of it what he said. How would you define it?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: By the end of the -- my involvement with Mr. Nikolic, I believe that most of what he had told us was the truth. However, I didn't believe in entirety that he had told us everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it -- do you know that he amended a lot of things he put in writing even, that he amended later?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Having a person like Mr. Momir Nikolic, why would we believe what he said if he is, as you said, an evasive person?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Sorry, could you just rephrase that. I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. You confirmed that he was evasive.

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why would we trust what he said, this Court, if even you characterised him as evasive?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Well, I'll leave that up to the Court to decide whether to believe that. As I said, my job was just to uncover the truth. So where he was being evasive, we would challenge him on that and try to get to the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm sorry that I bugged you with something that you don't deem necessary fit to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think the question was unfit and therefore, apparently, the witness better understood that than you did. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I don't understand my questions. That's not good, I think. I think I do but I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, you acted based on some rules, is that correct, as an investigator for the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the existence of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just read the entry portion of Rule 43, and I'll ask you something about that. So Rule 43, "Recording Questioning of Suspects," this rule was adopted in 1994. I quote: "Whenever the Prosecutor questions a suspect, the questioning shall be audio-recorded or video-recorded in accordance with the following procedure," and there is all set of rules. My question to you: Were you aware at that time that Rule 43 existed?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you understand its requirements?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask a question. Sir, were you an investigator or were you a Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An investigator, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have D301 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, are you familiar with this statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to be fair to you, can we see the last page of this document, please. As we can see, it's signed on the 6th of May, 2003, signed by Momir Nikolic. At the end, Momir Nikolic made corrections to paragraphs 10, then 9 and 10, and it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we see the paragraphs, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on the bottom of the page, Your Honour. I will go back to the paragraphs. It says: "In relation to the amended rejoinder indictment, Annex A, Momir Nikolic and the Office of the Prosecutor, I would like to make the following corrections," and it says, "paragraph 10, paragraphs 9 and 10," and it says, "paragraphs 11 and 45." Although there was only, I think, 15 paragraphs in that statement. And it says, "paragraph 46.6." First, I will ask you about this document. To your best knowledge, did Momir Nikolic correct his statement of facts at the end as we can see from this document; and did he personally provide corrections?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't -- I know he did make amendments, but I was not present during those amendments. But I did have access to the documents afterwards and then learned that he had made amendments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who decided what should be corrected? Momir Nikolic or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Again, I can't say whether it was himself or someone else, but I believe that the statement of facts was read over to him according to normal procedure with his Defence counsel at the time. So I presume the amendment would have been made by himself through his counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have in this document page 4 in both versions. We need paragraph 9, as we can see on our screens. We need paragraph 5 of this number 9, which starts with "I was at Konjevic Polje," and I will read this paragraph. "I was at Konjevic Polje for approximately 45 minutes before General Mladic arrived. His car arrived from the direction of Bratunac and stopped at the intersection at Konjevic Polje. He got out of his vehicle and we met in the middle of the road. I reported to him that there were no problems. He looked around and saw ... prisoners. Some of the prisoners asked him what would happen, to which he responded that they would all be transported away and they should not worry." Then, as we can see in the same paragraph, he talks about something that happened after General Mladic left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One little mistake while reading, Mr. Lukic. The sentence "he looked around and saw the prisoners," you left out the term "the."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Not just "prisoners," but "the prisoners."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we go back to the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that he corrected paragraph 9 and in these corrections, we do not need -- see any corrections in relation to General Mladic. So do you have any knowledge that somebody prevented Momir Nikolic from correcting part of his statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about anyone preventing him from making any corrections at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see D300 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And while we are waiting, Mr. Bursik, for this document, I just want to -- we had some discussion this morning so I want to clarify something. Did the Defence provide you with a binder of documents?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes. On my arrival in The Hague, I was provided with a binder of these documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When was it?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I arrived late evening on the 7th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the Defence provide you with the specific portions of those documents that we were discussing in this court?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes. And certain documents, certain sections were, I would say, highlighted by way of a covering letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In front of us, we have a statement, and in brackets, it says "Supplementary Statement." On the left-hand side, it says, "Momir Nikolic, prison, Finland." Did you have a chance to check how many paragraphs from the original statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility Mr. Nikolic corrected in this supplementary statement?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did read through the document, but I didn't count the number of corrections that he had made. But there were quite a few.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Lukic, is there any -- oh, let me just check.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We counted. He corrected 12 out of 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I was just looking at the previous document. That was a document which is from 2003. And what I see is that the English translation of this document does not include the header --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the facsimile header.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page, please. We can see on the last page that the corrections were made on the 16th of April, 2009.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. So we have now a better time-frame for both the documents. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have page 3 in English and page 6 in B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page in English version and top part of the B/C/S version, we see that Mr. Nikolic was discussing paragraph 9 on the statement and he would quote even sentences he was correcting from the previous document, and we have it under quotations marks. For example, we have under quotation marks: "I directed the work of the forces present in Potocari." And it's the last sentence from the first paragraph of paragraph 9 from his original statement. And then he would give the explanation. Would you agree -- actually, did Mr. Nikolic, Momir Nikolic, in his supplemental statement, correct his part in regard of General Mladic or anywhere else in this document? Did you have a chance to check?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I did not notice that he made any corrections with regard to General Mladic, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this was before -- this was after his testimony in Blagojevic trial. And before he testified in Blagojevic, he gave a statement to Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I will kindly ask to have 65 ter 25934 on our screens, please. This is the interview Momir Nikolic gave to Mr. Ruez on the 15th of December, 1999. And we need page 59, please. I cannot give you the correct page in B/C/S. I didn't work with B/C/S, but it's line 24 in English version, and it says -- it was recorded that Momir Nikolic said, I quote: "I saw Mladic on one occasion, I think it was one day after the fall of Srebrenica, and it was when he was supposed to negotiate with General Karremans. After that, I haven't seen him."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question to you, Mr. Bursik, is during your conversations, have you confronted Momir Nikolic with this statement of his?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I never directly confronted him with this previous statement about Mladic. The information that he gave about Mladic during my interview he gave voluntarily, so I didn't -- it wasn't as a result of a confrontation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we go back now to D300, please. It is supplementary statement to his -- to Momir Nikolic's statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility from 16th of April, 2009, and we'll need page 5 in English and page 7 in B/C/S. So we'll see the part that explains paragraph 12 from the statement of facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document written by his hand --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need page 5 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar informs me that we have only four pages in English, and that is what I see on e-court as well, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It refers to paragraphs --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My mistake. I stand corrected, Your Honours. It's page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 4, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in the second part of the page we see paragraph 12 discussed. And it says, I quote: "From 14th of July through October 1995, Bratunac Brigade forces, working with the MUP and the other VRS forces, continued to capture and execute Muslim prisoners attempting to escape from the Srebrenica and Zepa areas." And then he says, I quote: "Forces of the Bratunac Brigade took part in searching the terrain independently and, as far as I know, on one occasion together with MUP forces. I myself did not take part in these activities and I do not know what happened in the field, but all those captured by the Bratunac Brigade and brought to the brigade building [sic] were not killed, but were transferred by order of the Drina Corps Command to prison institutions in Batkovici, Vlasenica and Knezina."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you finish your question, where you earlier left out reading the word "the," now you included the word "the" in your first quote. "The other VRS forces" where it says -- no, let me see, "on one occasion together with MUP forces" and not "the MUP forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Obviously, I play with articles too much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's -- but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, have you ever checked this part of Momir Nikolic's statement, and if you know when, can you tell us when?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't understand your question. Which statement was I supposed to have checked?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, have you ever had this kind of information received from Momir Nikolic by the time you were with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: To be honest, Your Honour, I can't recall the specific information. It may have come up in some form of context but I can't independently recall this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Thank you. My question is maybe too general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, where I earlier corrected you, it was not about "the MUP forces" but about "other VRS forces," and not "the other VRS forces." So I made a small mistake there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have 1D1005 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is your information report, Mr. Bursik, as it says, composed on 23rd of June, 2003. At this moment, I will ask you about one fact from page 4 of English version, and it's -- it's actually the second-last paragraph on page 4, English version, and we need page 5 in B/C/S version. It's the first paragraph. The second-last paragraph says: "Nikolic estimates that there were about 120 opportunistic killings in Bratunac during this period and estimates the total amount of prisoners [sic] killed in the Bratunac area during that time is 2500 to 3500." Did you have the opportunity to check and do you believe it to be true today that in Bratunac area up to 3500 Muslim prisoners were killed?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: At that time, I never corroborated that evidence. And to the second part of your question, I believe this number to be a little bit exaggerated if you take into context what information we had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will move now to P1503.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, in front of us is declaration of Momir Nikolic from 6th of May, 2003. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document, Momir Nikolic admitted that he previously lied to the Prosecution. Did you have any role in composing or -- this document or questioning Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: No, I neither compiled this document nor confronted Nikolic on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document, he stated, I quote: "I made the false statements because I wrongly and inappropriately believed at the time that they would assist me in obtaining a plea agreement." Does this fit into your understanding of the personality of Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to 1D1005, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We saw this document a few moments ago, and we will stay with it for a while now. This is your document?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need page 8 in English for now, paragraph 7, and page 8, paragraph 7, in B/C/S as well. It's the second-last paragraph on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it reads, I quote: "Nikolic states that he was at the Kravica warehouse on the 13th of July (later retracted this) and ordered the execution there." Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have to go to page 1. Please, to go back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this date on this document - 23rd of June, 2003 - correct or not? Is this document composed on this date or not?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I believe it to be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph, under word or words "Information," entered twice, it was entered the following, and I quote: "On the 28th, 29th and 30th of May 2003, I together with Senior Trial Attorney, Peter McCloskey, interviewed Momir Nikolic in the United Nations Detention Facility in The Hague." Are those dates correctly entered in this document?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately, not. These were the incorrect dates. It was actually the 28th and 29th of April and I believe the 1st of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll come back to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have to go back to page 8 in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the second-last paragraph, I quote: "Nikolic states that he was at the Kravica warehouse on the 13th of July (later retracted this) and ordered the execution there. He said that Borovcanin arrived whilst the executions were [sic] under way and they spoke about what they should do about the bodies of those executed. Borovcanin did nothing to stop the shooting while he was there. Nikolic states that he had given the order to kill the prisoners after a prisoner had killed one of the guards. Borovcanin was aware that Nikolic had given the execution order. During this time, women and children were passing by in buses." In this part, Nikolic implied Borovcanin knew that Nikolic had given the execution order. Have you taken with a grain of salt allegations made by Momir Nikolic at the expense of others or did you simply record them?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: At the time of the interview, we just recorded it, until we could either corroborate his version or refute it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So do you know, did he later retract this part of his testimony?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware that he retracted this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this information report, it was said today that it was composed -- in this report, actually, it was said that it was composed based on the interviews you had with Mr. Momir Nikolic on the 28th, 29th and 30th of May, 2003, and we do have recordings from those dates. Today --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just a -- Your Honour, just a correction, and I'm sure this was inadvertent. The witness said 28th, 29th and 1st of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking about the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document says 30th of May, and that's what Mr. Lukic is quoting and, therefore, there was no need to intervene. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And we have it uploaded, all those three days, and 12th of June, 2003, also interview with Mr. Nikolic, as 1D06082.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Today you told us that, actually, there is a mistake in this report and those dates were not correct but that you had conversations with Mr. Nikolic on the 28th, 29th of April, and you believe 1st of May, 2003; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do we have recordings of those conversations?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: No, those -- that conversation was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You visited Mr. Momir Nikolic in the UN Detention Unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know at that time that Momir Nikolic was a suspect?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who decided --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was he a suspect or was he an accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time probably already accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking the witness because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Suspect because the Rule 43 talks about suspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know that. But was he a suspect or an accused at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believed he was an accused person. He had already been arrested and detained, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe it was just before the trial has to commence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you need to be an accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, before the break, I have -- we have time for one more question. Can you tell us who decided that you were not going to record your conversation with a suspect or at the time already accused Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: It was a joint decision that was reached between myself and Peter McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's time for a break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is, indeed, time for a break. Before we take that break, however, I would have one additional question. Late April and the 1st of May, the interview was not recorded, if I understand. Now, in this document, although giving the wrong dates, it says that Defence counsel were present during that interview. Could you tell us whether, on the -- the late April/1st of May interviews, were counsel present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recorded the names in the notes. I can't remember if both his counsel were present, but on this particular occasion in April, both Stephan Kirsh and Veselin Londrovic were present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I think Judge Moloto also has one more question before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, a little earlier when you were first shown this document, you agreed that these dates are incorrect, that they should have been 28th, 29th of April and 1st of May. Now, as the discussion goes on, it seems as if there are two separate recordings, the recordings on this date -- these dates and the recordings of the 28th, 29th and 1st of May. Am I right to say so or is this just one recording incorrectly dated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document that we're looking at now which covers the period the 28th, 29th and the 1st of -- 28th and 29th of April and 1st of May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not the document you're looking at, the 28th, 29th and 30th May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Excuse me, Your Honour. Yes, that's what it says on the document but I had made an error and put the incorrect dates on this document. So, in fact, there's two interviews that we are talking about. The first one took place more or less in the same days in April and the second one also on the 28th and 29th of May, so there was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Two separate interviews.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- two separate interviews. And therein lies the confusion about why I put the incorrect dates on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now I know. I'm clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the second one was recorded; the first one was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first one was not recorded, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We take a break, but we first invite you to follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, may I please interrupt and just ask one more clarification. Mr. Bursik, you indicated before the break that the decision not to record the interview or the conversation you had with Mr. Nikolic was taken by you and Mr. McCloskey. Am I correct that Defence counsel was present at that time in the discussion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. During the decision-making process as to whether to record it or not, they were not present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see. And he didn't play any part at the time when the proceedings of the interview began, to say -- to ask about the recording.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The Defence never raised a recording during the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, Rule 43 again that deals with recording questioning of suspects, in (vi), the last letter in that rule says: "The tape shall be transcribed if the suspect becomes an accused." Today we established that Momir Nikolic was already accused at that time. So was there any plan how to rectify this omission?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Well, we had an interview after the initial meetings with Mr. Nikolic. If I can perhaps explain a little bit further, going into this interview with Mr. Nikolic, it was going into the whole plea bargaining process where we were going to reach a plea agreement, so it was not the normal suspect interview or accused interview as what would appear. But, in hindsight, looking at it now, I perhaps made an error of judgement and I take full responsibility for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us just now that you had an interview after these initial meetings with Mr. Nikolic. And do you consider that the subsequent interviews that were recorded actually rectify the omissions for not recording the first conversations?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: The second interview was not going to rectify the omission from the first. It was just a subsequent interview to glean more information and get a better understanding of what Mr. Nikolic knew or didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We'll come to that interview. I'll ask you now in connection with the first one, this one you told us today was in April. What did you consider the purpose of not recording the conversation to be?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: As I said in the particular approach made to Mr. Nikolic it was with a view of exploring the possibility of a plea agreement. So the decision was made that it would not be the normal suspect or accused interview and it would more be a discussion into what he knew, what he would admit to, what he would not admit to. But, at the same time, I thought it would be important to record by way of notes what he was saying at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many times have you questioned a suspect or an accused without recording the questioning?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: For the Office of the Prosecutor, while I was here at the ICTY, I think there was one or two occasions with similar circumstances, but I cannot independently recall who the other person was. But I don't think it was the only occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You just told us that you cannot recall. Can you inform us later in which occasion you did not record the interview with the suspect or the accused?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I don't think I'll be able to tell you later because I cannot remember. But it probably would have been in a similar circumstance, for example, into the initial discussions toward a plea agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To your best knowledge, would that be against the rules as well?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: In hindsight, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Against what rule exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Rule 43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is about suspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which is about accused as well. I just read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. It said that transcription should be made if a person becomes an accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should accused have less rights than a suspect? No, I need --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. You can ask questions of fact. You introduced in your last question, leading, that it was against the rules, and I asked you which rule you had on your mind. That's it. Whether or not that rule also implicates that an accused interview should also be -- at this moment the Chamber is just intervening in a question which states something, and the Chamber would certainly not express itself on that matter without having heard both parties. And, therefore, for your examination of the witness at this moment, ask questions. This is a witness of fact. Ask questions as you deem fit. I just sought a short clarification of something you put as a legal opinion in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is Rule 49 as well that talks about interviewing and taping, although it says "may," of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you are now continuing a legal debate, Mr. Lukic, where I said that I thought it inappropriate at this moment. I mean, if you apply rules on interviewing witnesses in a situation where someone is a suspect or an accused, you would have other problems as well. So the matter is too complex, and for a witness of fact, you don't need this guidance. You may ask the witness what he feels about it, but if you introduce in your question a legal opinion, then the only thing I did is ask if you refer to a rule, what rule. That's the one and only thing I did. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Being an experienced investigator, Mr. Bursik, how do you understood the police position of Mr. Nikolic? Would he have less rights than a suspect or at least similar rights as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I would say he had the same rights as a suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many times did you question Momir Nikolic without recording the interview?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I can only recall on these three occasions. The other interviews that we had afterwards were recorded. If I can perhaps clarify where I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So maybe I will repeat the question but I don't think that I got a clear answer. What made you conduct these three interviews on the 28th, 29th of April and 1st of May differently from how you would usually conduct them?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: On this occasion, we were exploring what Mr. Nikolic would admit to or what he would not admit to with a view to entering into a plea agreement, so it was different, in my mind, to a normal suspect or an accused interview. It was an interview, perhaps one could say, of [Realtime transcript read in error "explosion"] exploration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. We saw your report consists of 14 pages with some pictures at the end after those 14 pages. During those three days, was anybody else taking notes; do you know?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Nikolic himself took a few notes, and as far as I can recall, his legal counsel also took some notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Were you able to obtain those notes from Mr. Nikolic and his counsel?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: No, but I never asked for them either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ask the same questions in your interviews of 28th, 29th and 30th May, 2003 as you did in the earlier interviews from April and 1st of May?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: There were some grounds of overlap between the two interviews, but it would be incorrect to say that I asked the same questions because we had already covered some of the ground in the first interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll direct your attention now to that movement that was said that Momir Nikolic explained that General Mladic made. You include that in your report from 23rd of June, 2003. Would you consider it important?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, I believe the hand motion made to him during the interview was important and that's the reason why I recorded it in the information report, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you, then, why didn't you ask him about it during recorded conversation in order to have it on the record?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: As I said earlier, we did have areas of overlap, but it never came up in conversation again, as far as I'm aware, during the recorded interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who asked you to prepare this information report?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: It was a member of the trial team at the time, but I cannot independently recall which member of the trial team asked me to type out my notes that I'd made on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "trial team," you mean trial team from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The trial team dealing with Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you understand the purpose of producing this document to be?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: My understanding was that we could get what Mr. Nikolic had said onto the evidential system so that it would not be lost in the lapse of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you consider recorded statement by Mr. Nikolic to be more reliable than these notes?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Obviously a recording is extremely reliable because it records every word, whereas notes are prone to human error as can you see by my dates -- my incorrect dates in the first opening sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then you produced the addendum to this; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that before your report it has never been recorded that Momir Nikolic described his encounter with General Mladic in Konjevic Polje on the 13th of July, 1995 in a way that he said that Mladic turned and gestured with his hand with a flat wave and that he understood it to mean that the prisoners were to be killed?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: It's my recollection that was the first time I'd ever heard it, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While you're preparing, Mr. Lukic, I just revisit for one second our earlier discussion. When I asked you what rule, I was, rather, thinking not in terms of Rule 43 or only indirect in relation to Rule 43 but I was thinking -- I would not have been surprised if would you have said Rule 63 which is about questioning of an accused, and refers to Article 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right. My questions were composed based on believing that Mr. Nikolic was a suspect at that time, but I was corrected today and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And now perhaps I led you also to the applicable rule which then again refers to Rule 43. But I wanted to have matters perfectly clear in this respect, and I did not - and still do not - start a debate at this moment. Just to assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can have D300 on our screens, please, again. We had it before. It is supplementary statement by Momir Nikolic. I will skip several questions since I think that I got the answers already. So I will call 65 ter 18558, please. This is your document that contains both B/C/S and English versions, so we'll deal with English version so that the witness can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During your conversations with Momir Nikolic, were you aware that in 1987 criminal proceedings were instigated against Momir Nikolic in former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I cannot independently recall whether this information was at my disposal at that time, but the probability was that it was at my disposal because we had an analyst team which worked on documentation to prepare us for interviews. So it probably was in the information bundle that I had, but I cannot independently recall having this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document, it was recorded that the whole case file does not exist in the police as it had disappeared at an unidentified point in time, under unclear circumstances. Do you have any knowledge whether Momir Nikolic had any dealings with destruction of these documents?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I have no knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it refers to Article 167 of the Criminal Code of the SFRY, the version of 1987. If you could ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was about to ask you, Mr. Lukic, whether you remember, because I do not, what Article 167, paragraph 1, stands; and if you say so, then the Prosecution could consider whether they agree with you, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll check it. I'm consulting with my colleague, Stojanovic. It could be that it was some forgery of a cheque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Forgery. Thank you. The parties are invited to read what it is, unless you further deal with it yourself. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Moving now from this to D01018. So if we can have this one on our screens. We need 1D01018.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is supplemental information sheet from the 23rd of October, 2007. You were not in the Tribunal at that time anymore. But I'll direct your attention, as I already did previously, to page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need bullet point 5 from the top, and page 3 in B/C/S, point 3 from the top. It is -- now we don't see the top of the page, but it is in English version the second bullet point from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it says, I quote: "The witness stated that although he did destroy documents, including documents which were about the Srebrenica campaign, he did not destroy any documents from the security organ ..." During your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should complete the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "He did not destroy any documents from the security organ in violation of any applicable regulations on retention of documents." During your conversation with Mr. Nikolic, did you have any knowledge, did you hear from him that he was destroying documents in connection with Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I have no recollection of discussing the destruction of documents with him during my discussions with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you describe us how that whole process worked when you did not record conversation with Mr. Nikolic? Was anybody leaving the room? Was he sometimes alone with his lawyers or you were all the time together? How would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: No, we took frequent breaks and we allowed him alone-time with his lawyers. There were breaks for ablutions, breaks for smoking, for a number of reasons. So, yeah, there were frequent breaks during that time in which he was left alone with his counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably needless to say, but I would like to have it on the record, did you record those break times in your notes?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we --

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Sorry, if I can clarify. Are you referring to did I record the content of what was said during the breaks or did I record that we actually took breaks?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Content. Content. You understood me correctly.

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: No, we didn't record content. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to fully understand, during the breaks you were not with the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We were -- as I said, we would either go down the hall to take our ablutions or -- but he would either stay in the room with his counsel or him and his counsel would leave the room and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You also did not record when you took a break and how long that break lasted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my notes, my written notes, I would have recorded it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Last bullet point on this page, in the middle of the paragraph, the sentence starts with -- it's fifth row from the beginning of this bullet point. It says, and I will quote -- this was recorded by Mr. Julian Nicholls, as I said, on 23rd October 2007. "During a break when discussing Kravica his attorney Londrovic came in to speak with him alone and told him that unless he admitted responsibility for Kravica there would be no plea agreement. The witness stated that his attorney said that unless he did this there would be no possibility of ... plea agreement with Mr. McCloskey." Would you consider that [B/C/S on English channel].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We receive B/C/S on English channel. You can still understand it, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could I start from the beginning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please start your question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, would you consider this as a truthful statement uttered by Momir Nikolic or another lie?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I would not say it's a truthful statement. I did not overhear any such conditions that were being attached to this agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, may I remind that you're examining in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Another lie" is at least somewhat leading, isn't it? Would you please adhere to the rules where the subject matter of your examination is about sticking to the rules, isn't it? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So maybe it's too late but I try to rectify. My mistake. How would you understand this part of Momir Nikolic's statement to be?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I never ever heard his counsel say these words to him, so I can neither corroborate it or refute it. But what I can say is that there were no conditions. The only condition that we asked for was that he be open and honest with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just get clarity. Could we please look at the first page of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Can we have the first page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Bursik, you're answering the question as if you were present during this interview, but apparently you had left the Tribunal at the time and Mr. Lukic did say so when he put up this document on the screen. Do you have any knowledge of the content of this document to be able to answer these questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have knowledge only because it was -- I read through this document during my proofing session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. Reading the document, I understand. But I'm getting the impression that you're trying to explain what happened during breaks and what have you, but it doesn't seem like you were present during this interview. So you can't tell, for instance, what happened during breaks, can you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the document, although it is dated 2007, is referring to the interview which occurred in 2003. But I'll stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If that is the case, then I withdraw my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I maybe rushed too much, Your Honour. I will try to, again, rectify something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First bullet point on our screen says that the witness complained that the statement of facts filed as part of his guilty plea was not accurate as follows. And Mr. Bursik was right. Actually, in this document, it was his plea agreement discussed and he here complained in 2007 that his plea agreement was not correct, and there are some remarks from his side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bursik, one additional question. You said there were no conditions; he just had to tell us the truth. But if you believed that he was responsible for Kravica, then, of course, if he wouldn't admit that, you would consider him not to be truthful, and since that was a condition for the plea agreement, it's rather ambiguous on whether there were no conditions. He only had to tell the truth. If he would have told you that he was not responsible for anything, you would say, then, okay, we make a plea agreement on that; or if he would have said that he was guilty on minor points, you would not have entered into a plea agreement, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. If there were minor points that he was being a little bit evasive, we would still have carried on with the plea agreement. But what I was trying to say is that we did not go into specifics, and if you do not admit to X or Y or Z, we would not enter into an agreement. But it was quite clear that he was being a little bit evasive, and that's why we said to him and his counsel that we would request them to be open and truthful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you needed, in order to be convinced that that was the case, you needed a substantial admission of involvement and guilt at certain events.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you never said: "Without Kravica, no way." Without ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never said it, and I never overheard it being said, Your Honours, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And hinting at that? Sometimes you can hint at something without making it a condition.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It may have -- it may have been hinted or so, but to be honest, I can't recall that matter actually coming up in conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just another follow-up on the same question. According to this document, this suggestion that he must admit to Kravica was made not by you but by his counsel during a break, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And do you remember ever discussing whether this must be a condition either before or after -- before the break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were discussing the subject of Kravica during the interview, I believe, but it never came up during a break as a condition or anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We yesterday discussed some objections Momir Nikolic had regarding his plea agreement, so can we have 1D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean today -- oh, you discussed in proofing. Yes, okay. We're not privy of what you discussed in proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we need 1D01005 on our screens again. We talked today already about this document. Now we need page 11 in English, last paragraph, and page 12, third paragraph, in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document, it was recorded, I will read and I quote: "With regard to the activities in Potocari on the 12th of July, Nikolic states that he was not in charge of the units deployed there, but co-ordinated them. He states that these units had already been instructed what to do by their commanders." So let's focus on this "co-ordinate." Who chose the terminology used to describe the role of Momir Nikolic in his plea agreement?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Well, the terminology would come from Nikolic himself, obviously through an interpreter, but also in my report, I would then also go from my notes. So it's -- although Nikolic may have said that word himself, it would have been interpreted from B/C/S into English and then I would have recorded it down into how that sentence would read properly in my notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one thing: Veselin Londrovic, is he a native B/C/S-speaking person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does he speak any English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe Mr. Kirsh speaks English, but I don't think that Mr. Londrovic speaks any English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are not supposed to give testimony. But if that's the case, then, of course, I do understand that you would further explore it in the proper way. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, did you have the opportunity to speak in English with Mr. Londrovic?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Perhaps this will clarify Your Honour's question as well. He speaks very broken English. We used mostly the interpreter with him, but we were able to get by in very broken language.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose mine is the same, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Here the Chamber has to disagree, Mr. Lukic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we shortly now have D00300, please. This is supplementary statement from Mr. Nikolic. It's from 2009. And in his supplementary statement, on page 2 in English -- so we need page 2 in English, and there are comments with paragraph 4. It's second paragraph on this page. And, in B/C/S, it's page 3 in the middle of the page, also comments with paragraph 4. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Momir Nikolic wrote the following. Paragraph 4 of the statement, lines 11 to 12, paragraph 4, in brackets: "When I talked to the Office of the Prosecutor and until my trial ended, I paid no heed to formulations of this kind and I did not even know what military co-ordination actually and precisely meant." And the same, we have on other places in this document, like on English page 3, in comments with paragraph 6, we do not have to switch the page, just for the record. My question for you, Mr. Bursik, is: What was your impression? Did Mr. Momir Nikolic knew -- did he know the meaning of the terms he was using?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: My interpretation of it is that he did, indeed, know what he was talking about and that he knew what the words were. He continually, not often but he did make corrections which led me also to believe that he -- if there was fault, he was finding it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to compare the information we have in D301, which is statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility, and your information report, which is marked as 1D01005. Do you agree that there is a difference in between those recorded statements of Momir Nikolic, that in the plea agreement there was nothing about flat wave of General Mladic, unlike in your report?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: To the first part of your question, I agree there are discrepancies and changes were made. And I agree with your second question, that he made no reference to that in his statement of facts, about the motion of his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have now 1D06082 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can hear the voice of Mr. Mladic who is supposed to speak at non-audible volume.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, you were recorded here as having conversation with Momir Nikolic on this page on 28th of May, 2003. Is this recording of your -- do you remember? Did you have a chance to check it? Is this a recording of your conversations with Mr. Momir Nikolic in May?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, this is a transcript of the tape recordings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 61 from this document, please. Just for the record, it is recorded that this part took place on the 29th of May, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In his -- here, it was discussed, Mr. Momir Nikolic's statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility, and it was discussed about paragraph 9, as we can see, and in that paragraph, you already concluded that there was no flat wave made as a gesture by General Mladic. And you asked Mr. Nikolic, and I will quote from line 1: "Okay. Now, paragraph 9 talks a lot about what you did travelling along the road." Momir Nikolic: "Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask a question. Do the initials "PM" refer to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hear you saying "You asked."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To whom actually does "PM" correspond?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: The initials PM, Your Honour, refer to Peter McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So sorry for guiding you wrongly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for helping me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again it was recorded that Mr. McCloskey asked: "Going to Konjevic Polje, picking up the prisoners, is that all correct? Do you want to add or delete anything from that paragraph 9?" Momir Nikolic: "This is all correct." Was this correctly recorded?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, this is a direct transcript of the taped recording. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you told us today, you had conversation with Momir Nikolic on the 28th, 29th, and 1st -- 28th, 29th April and 1st of May, 2003, and it was your information report composed on the 23rd of June, 2003. Then we had the plea agreement reached on the 6th of May, 2003. And after that plea agreement, Mr. Nikolic was asked during this interview at the end of May 2003 if he wanted to correct anything in his plea agreement, paragraph 9, and he said everything was correct. Would you agree -- actually, I cannot lead you. This report, this recorded statement and plea agreement is different from your report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: There are errors of inconsistency, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Both plea agreement and this interview took part after your conversation with Momir Nikolic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, it took -- the plea agreement and conversation took place after the three initial days of meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the break time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It, indeed, is. Mr. Bursik, we'll take a break of 20 minutes. We'd like to see you back after the break. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at a quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, you are aware of the sentencing judgement in Momir Nikolic case, are you?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, but it's been many years since I've read it so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But do you know that the Trial Chamber, in paragraph 156 of that judgement, found about Momir Nikolic the same as you did; that in numerous instances the testimony of Momir Nikolic was evasive and the Chamber found this to be an indication that his willingness to co-operate does not translate into being fully forthcoming in relation to all the events given in his position and knowledge. Will you agree with this finding of the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I'm aware of the Trial Chamber's finding, although I cannot remember the specific paragraph but that's the gist of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not only leading [Realtime transcript read in error "misleading"], Mr. Lukic. It's also asking for an opinion, whether the witness agrees or does not agree with what a Trial Chamber says, not knowing what the deliberations are at the basis of that, are pretty useless. I mean, your point is perfectly clear. Let me be -- I mean, the point you make is clear. The way in which you do it is not the proper way. But please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I thought we had established already that Mr. Bursik spent a lot of time talking to Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But his opinions and his impressions -- and you didn't ask him -- and I didn't intervene at that point in time, you asked whether the witness agrees with what apparently is the outcome of the deliberations of that Chamber, not knowing what the basis of it is, and whether he agrees or disagrees is not of that much importance. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have 1D01018, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where the transcript reads "it's not only misleading," I didn't say "misleading." "It's not only leading," I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik, we already saw this document today in this courtroom and I would just like you to focus, although you were not present when this document was composed, and this part, I think, talks about 2007. The part I want to ask you is the last part of paragraph 2, fifth row from the bottom of that paragraph, and the sentence starts: "At the 27th September meeting, the witness pointed to a large number of handwritten notes and stated that these were private notes he had written in preparation for his Defence in his own trial. The witness has refused to allow the Prosecution to review these notes and will not provide the Prosecution with a copy of the notes." During your tenure and during your conversations with Mr. Nikolic, was he willing to share his notes with you?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: His willingness to share the notes never came into question because we never ever asked him for the notes because I regarded those to be confidential between him and his counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just in order to avoid whatever confusion, here, specific notes are referred to which he didn't want to give, made in preparation of his -- did you ever come across any notes he used or displayed although did not give access to? Was there any issue of notes being on the table when you interviewed him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Every time I interviewed Mr. Nikolic he had his own notes with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And he would make notes under his own hand. But at no stage did we ever ask him for a copy of those notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Apart from your notes composed on the 23rd of June, 2003, do you know when actually Mr. Nikolic mentioned this flat wave made by General Mladic for the first time?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: It was -- in my recollection, it was during those first three days of interview, although I cannot recall on which day he mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Those three days that were not recorded?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was after those three days, do you remember when he said that for the first time and that was recorded?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I can't recall when he said that, sir, subsequently to our discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would you accept that it was in the Blagojevic/Jokic trial in 2003?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: I'm sure it's a matter of being in the record. But, as I said, I can't recall it independently, him saying it during trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have now 1D06096, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is transcript from B and H State Court trial against Mitrovic, Petar, regarding Kravica, and it was testimony of Momir Nikolic via videolink on 6th of February, 2008. This means after plea agreement, after your notes, after the recorded testimony, after Blagojevic/Jokic trial. And we need page 22 from this transcript to see how here Mr. Nikolic explained the same situation. I can see it's highlighted from the line 14 to line 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Who did the highlighting, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I did, obviously, and somehow it was uploaded that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was recorded that OJ, and on the bottom of the page, we could see that it means Ozrenka Jaksic, asked, I quote: "How long did you stay in Konjevic Polje and why did you stay there? What was the reason for your departure to Konjevic Polje?" Momir Nikolic responded: "On that day General Mladic was supposed to pass through that route and my intention was to check if that road was operative, passable and secure. And I stayed there for, until General Mladic passed." "And did you then return in the direction of Bratunac?" Momir Nikolic: "Yes." I understand that you did not follow this trial, but have you ever checked or cross-checked other witness statements given to the OTP? Have you ever checked whether Momir Nikolic actually was at Konjevic Polje on the 13th of July, 1995? And I will direct you, for example, there is an interview conducted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, leading is one thing but then already to read --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't want to read. Just to mention the name, if the gentleman checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's refrain also from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you answer my question, or should I repeat it?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: You're asking me if we cross-checked whether he was in Konjevic Polje. All the aspects that Momir told us we tried to corroborate, but I cannot independently recall whether we actually found someone who put him in Konjevic Polje on the 13th. There may have been, but I, to be honest, can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you then ever find someone who contradicted or gave evidence contrary to that he would have been in Konjevic Polje on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall anyone giving any evidence to show that he wasn't in Konjevic Polje either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, the Prosecution conducted an interview with Mr. Andric, Pero, on the 20th of February, 2002, and there were some other witnesses but you responded already to my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that would refresh the memory of the witness, there's nothing wrong with asking him where he said he has no recollection, whether this refreshes his memory. Are you aware of an interview Mr. Pero Andric, February 2002?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The name sounds familiar to me, Your Honour, but this was about 13 years ago and so I cannot remember interviewing him or reading his interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This was my last question. I would just like to thank Mr. Bursik for answering our questions, and I would offer the documents I was using today, although probably we would upload shorter versions of the transcripts. There is no need for the whole transcript to be uploaded. And if the Prosecution deems it necessary, they can add any page they want. And I would just read now 65 ter numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, first of all, is there any objection to any of those documents that were shown to the witness and were brought to our screens, any objection against admission?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, some of the documents were interviews of Momir Nikolic and I think portions of those were read. I'm not entirely in agreement that the entire transcript needs to go in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But that's what Mr. Lukic, I think, says, that he wants to make a further selection. Because what I'm seeking to have happen is that Mr. Lukic now has apparently prepared or is still prepares excerpts of the documents relevant for what he used and read to the witness, to the extent necessary. Then if the Prosecution would like to deal with the same documents - I don't know whether you intend to refer to any of those documents, Ms. Hasan - that you'd come to a joint -- do a joint submission, more or less, of what gives sufficient context.
