And if the parties could agree that if it's a very small portion where it is only read into the transcript so that there's no need -- if it is accurately read into the transcript, that there is no need at all to tender it, to try to condense everything and get everything well organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. I have three documents that -- documents, not transcripts. I could offer them immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we need them in their entirety?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think so. It's short documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Short documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- composed by Mr. Bursik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then -- but there is no basic objection against the use of those documents, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we just know which three Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no. We'll deal with those. But with any other ones, transcripts --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We'll work on it with Mr. Lukic once he gets the excerpts together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's appreciated. Then the three short documents, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. They are 1D01005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you say what it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's information report composed by Mr. Bursik on 23rd June, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D01005 receives Exhibit D1228, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Next one is 65 ter 18558.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Information regarding destruction of criminal file against Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Short message from the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 18558 receives Exhibit D1229, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the next one is supplemental information sheet, composed by Julian Nicholls. As I understand it, it's a three-page document and bears the number 1D01018.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, I hear of no objections. Therefore, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D01018 receives Exhibit D1230, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. And the parties will further consider what excerpts --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe it would be wise to tell the Prosecution which are the remaining three so they can work on them as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first one is 1D06082. That is a conversation between Mr. Bursik and Momir Nikolic on 28th of May, 29th of May, 30th of May, and 12th of June, 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the recorded interview. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next one is 1D06096. It's a transcript from Bosnian court, so testimony, in 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the 67-page document. At this moment you will find excerpts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. And the last one is 65 ter number 25934 which is an interview conducted between Mr. Ruez and Momir Nikolic on the 15th of December, 1999, so that predates what Mr. Bursik was part of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the Chamber expects to be informed about what excerpts finally are tendered. Mr. Lukic, thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bursik.

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just to introduce myself, my name is Abir Hasan and I'll ask you questions on behalf of the Prosecution. Now, just as a point of clarification, if we could take a look at D -- what is now D1228 and that's your information report from -- dated the 23rd of June, 2003. Now, you were asked by Defence counsel a question comparing the statement of facts with your info report. This is at transcript page 40. So you'll understand this clearly, if you look at paragraph 2 of that information report, you write: "This information report sets forth the content of the interview not included in the statement of facts as signed by Momir Nikolic as part of the plea agreement. It should thus be read together with the statement of facts for a comprehensive overview of the interview in its entirety."

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And the interview you are referring to here, am I correct, that that's the plea discussion interviews which took place on the 28th and 29th of April, and the 1st of May?

utterances.speaker: BRUCE BURSIK
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN

The Defence objected to the admission, stating, inter alia, that the witness had no knowledge about the document. This to be found on transcript pages 28478 to -481. The Prosecution subsequently tendered this document during the testimony of Drasko Vujic on the 4th of May, 2015. The Defence objected again to admission, stating that Witness Vujic had no knowledge of the document and that the content of the document is not linked to his testimony. The Chamber recalls that the applicable law for the admission of evidence is set out in Rule 89(C) of the Rules which allows a chamber to admit any relevant evidence which it deems to have probative value. With regard to the Defence's objection that the witnesses had no knowledge about the document, the Chamber recalls its prior practice that a document's probative value can also be established if its content is sufficiently linked to the content of the witness's statement. The Chamber considers the relevance of the article and finds that it relates to the charges in the municipalities' component of the case. The Chamber further considers that Witness Corokalo had no knowledge of the document and finds that as he also did not testify about the content of the article, the content of the document is insufficiently linked to his testimony. Witness Vujic testified in general terms that many non-Serbs left Prijedor but that he had no knowledge of the circumstances under which they left. He testified in detail about non-Serbs leaving Puharska in 1992/1993. The article, however, deals with the alleged expulsion of about 5.000 non-Serbs from the Prijedor area in 1995, and the Chamber therefore finds that the content of the article is insufficiently linked to his testimony and therefore denies the admission of P6925.
